fixes.row: The Lord's table: blood “poured out”, “in remembrance of Me”, “a participation”
fixes.why: The row takes the cup and blood words and the memorial words, but leaves out the bread-and-body words of the Matthew and Mark institution accounts (Matt 26:26 'this is My body'; Mark 14:22) and Heb 13:10 'We have an altar', which the note itself names as left out to hold to the card's own graph. That is a selection made for the graph, not for the text, and it tilts the row toward a memorial reading that these seats would see as cutting the text short.
fixes.fix: Add Matt.26.26, Mark.14.22 and Heb.13.10 to the row (Heb 13:10 needs no card word, so mark it in the note as read beside the table), and drop the note's sentence about holding to what the graph backs. Keep the no-side note.

fixes.row: Sacrifice and sin: the sin offering, the guilt offering, “for sins”
fixes.why: The note says Heb 10:26 'stands here with Heb 10:12 and 10:18', but neither 10:18 nor 10:26 is in this row's verse list (10:26 is not in any row that the list shows). A reader who looks for the verses the note names will not find them, and the hard verse on falling away is cited without being shown under the heading that carries it.
fixes.fix: Add Heb.10.18 (offering, prosphora) and Heb.10.26 (sacrifice, thysia) to the row's verses, so the note's citations are on the page. Keep the note's statement that the page takes no side on whether a believer can fall away.

fixes.why: Rule 6 asks every example to show its label. The two New Testament examples in the row's four (Eph 5:2 and Phil 4:18) print 'fragrant sacrificial offering' and 'fragrant offering'; the words 'pleasing aroma' do not appear in them. The note explains the link, but the example does not show the label. Only 2 of this row's 4 examples show it.
fixes.fix: Relabel to 'A pleasing or fragrant aroma (the offering as a fragrance)' so both English forms are shown, or swap Eph.5.2 and Phil.4.18 out of the four examples for two verses that print 'pleasing aroma' and move them to the note.

worker_points.point: 1. What a sacrifice does (aroma, atonement made, blood, without blemish, eating, sin rows); notes say the page takes no side
worker_points.why: Each contested reading is named in the note and no row order settles it; 'he will be forgiven' is quoted from the verse, not stated as the page's own view, so it does not tilt penal or ritual. Covered under the seats' own readings.

worker_points.point: 2. Fulfilled, ended or continued (rows 'Sacrifice set beside what the LORD asks', 'Sacrifice in days to come', 'Offered again and again', and the gift-at-the-altar verb row)
worker_points.why: The Old Testament statements and the Hebrews statements sit together with notes that name the readings and the point of dispute. Hebrews and Ezekiel are not set against each other by row order. The Amos 5:25 question was moved out of the statement row, which was right.

worker_points.point: 3. Jer 7:22: the Berean's 'merely' has no Hebrew word
worker_points.why: The note states it and sends the matter to a translation finding. It is a true statement about the translation and it does not favour any seat. The translation question itself belongs in the findings file, not in the reader's note, but this is not a reason to fix the row.

worker_points.point: 4. The Lord's Supper row: widen, keep, or drop
worker_points.why: Keep the row, but widen it. Only 1 Cor 10:18 has a sacrifice word, so the row is kept by the card's graph alone; the institution words of Matthew and Mark and Heb 13:10 are the verses the Catholic, Eastern Orthodox and Lutheran seats would look for. Dropping the row would be a tilt the other way. See fix 1.

worker_points.point: 5. Christ's sacrifice by hand (Heb 7:27, 9:25, 10:12 'He', 'this Priest'; Heb 9:14, 9:28, 1 Cor 5:7 name Christ)
worker_points.why: The row label names Christ and the verses that say 'He' are inside the same letter where Jesus is named (Heb 10:10). That is the text's own reference, and the note does not invent a dispute about who is meant. The divine persons are not placed by rule.

worker_points.point: 6. Eating from the sacrifice as communion (Lev 7:15; 1 Cor 8:10; 10:18; Rev 2:14, 20; Ezek 39:17-19; Hos 9:4)
worker_points.why: The four examples show the label, the hard verses are named as hard, and the note says readers part on what the meal means. No seat is placed above another.

worker_points.point: 7. Heb 10:26 ('no further sacrifice for sins remains') under 'Sacrifice and sin'
worker_points.why: The statement is right to keep, but the row's verse list does not contain Heb 10:26 or 10:18 although the note says they stand there. See fix 2.

worker_points.point: 8. Isaac (Heb 11:17 and Jas 2:21 under 'offer him as a burnt offering')
worker_points.why: James 2:21 sits inside the faith and works argument, and the note refers the reader to the faith page and names the readings of the story. The Reformed and Lutheran seats would be satisfied that the note does not decide faith and works here.

worker_points.point: 9. Children given in sacrifice (2 Kgs 3:27; Ps 106:37-38; Jer 19:5; Ezek 16:20)
worker_points.why: Hard verses are kept and named as Israel's sin and the worship of Baal, and the note says Isaac is the row above. Judg 11:31 sits only in the catch-all, which is acceptable for a single unnamed vow. No seat is misled.

worker_points.point: 10. Other gods and idols: Paul on food sacrificed to idols beside Naaman's vow (2 Kgs 5:17)
worker_points.why: The row names what the verses are about and the note does not characterise Paul's argument in 1 Cor 8-10. The rabbi would see the Naaman verse kept on its own terms.

worker_points.point: 11. The prophets' 'sacrifice of the LORD' (Isa 34:6; Jer 46:10; Ezek 39:17-19) kept in blood and eating rows
worker_points.why: Kept where the text puts them, named in notes, and not made into a doctrine of judgment; the hard verses stay visible.

worker_points.point: 12. Divine persons: nothing placed by rule
worker_points.why: No row is organised by who the subject is. 'Christ offered Himself' is a picked row with the verses the text gives, which meets rule 3.

missing.what: The Lord's table: the institution words of Matthew and Mark ('this is My body'), which the Catholic, Eastern Orthodox and Lutheran seats expect beside the blood words. Included in fix 1, listed here so the gap is visible.

The altar of Heb 13:10, which the Catholic and Eastern Orthodox seats read with the Lord's table and the sacrifice of Christ. Heb 13:10 contains no card word; the worker's note said it was left out for that reason. Panel to say whether to keep it out, and if so name it in the note.

John 1:29, 'Look, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world': the lamb-sacrifice image most readers across the traditions would look for under 'Christ offered Himself'. It has no card word (it is the card's lamb image, not a sacrifice word), so the row rule does not reach it; a note or a row on the Lamb of God would show the link to the Passover row.

examples_checked: 23 of 24 rows: every example shows its label; 'A pleasing aroma' shows it in 2 of 4 (Eph 5:2 and Phil 4:18 print 'fragrant').
summary: The hub is sound: each contested reading is named in a note that takes no side, the Old Testament is heard on its own terms first, and the divine persons are not placed by rule. It should ship after three fixes: widen the Lord's table row with the body words and Heb 13:10, put the verses that the Heb 10:18 and 10:26 note names into their row, and relabel the aroma row so its examples show its label.
